aid.value: International admission is explicitly need-aware. Merit and variable need-based aid are available, not universal full-cost coverage. Submit the free portal Non-US Citizen aid form instead of CSS within days of the admission application; priority February 1. Qualifying need support can last eight semesters; financial certification before enrollment remains separate. Alfond has separate fall first-year eligibility: ED I/EA with all materials by November 15, at most two gap years, competitive interviews; spring/transfer applicants excluded. It covers tuition, room/board, not insurance/books/personal/taxes; international recipients need roughly $6,000–8,000 for residual expenses. Details: https://www.rollins.edu/scholarships-aid/scholarships/alfond-scholars-program/faq/

attributes.aidShort: Need-aware partial aid; competitive Alfond has residual costs

evidence.quote: Rollins takes into account a family’s contribution

testing.value: International applicants can submit official SAT/ACT scores or apply test-optional. This does not waive English proficiency; test-optional first-year applicants remain eligible for the competitive Alfond award, subject to its separate requirements.

english.value: Older TOEFL minimum 80 before January 21, 2026; new minimum 4.5 after that date, IELTS 6.5 or DET 120. Confirm the transition-day wording for an exam taken on January 21. Waiver: SAT critical reading 550 or recent English-medium school transcripts covering at least two years. Official IELTS must be delivered electronically by the test center, not paper reports; DET results must also be officially shared.

evidence.quote: IELTS: an overall band score of 6.5

fee.value: Both the Rollins application and Common App routes are free for international admission. The free financial-aid form is separate; visa, testing, document and enrollment expenses are not automatically waived.

deadline.value: The international timetable lists ED II January 5, while the first-year ED FAQ says January 6: https://www.rollins.edu/apply/first-time/faqs/early-decision/ . Confirm the intake and ED II date; do not silently choose the later one. Both sources have ED I/EA November 15; international RD February 1 and spring December 10 are listed without entry-year labels. Alfond requires all materials November 15, earlier than the generic EA supporting-document December 1 instruction. The international FAQ's blanket February 1 statement should not override earlier rounds or Alfond eligibility.

evidence.quote: Early Decision Round 2 Apply By January 5

aid.value: International students receive merit consideration, not need-based aid, but the international aid page gives inconsistent first-year merit ceilings: $30,000 in the introduction versus $33,000 in its detailed award section and undergraduate overview. Confirm the current amount and renewal conditions rather than assigning an exact guaranteed net cost. Its approximate $73,559 cost is explicitly 2026–27, not a future-year quote. Distinguished Scholar is a separate competitive application covering tuition, specified fees and room/board, excluding health insurance; it supersedes ordinary merit. Transfer/adult awards and eligibility are separate. No CSS-based international need aid is implied by generic Common App tags.

evidence.quote: these scholarships range from $16,000 to 30,000 per year

testing.value: Simmons' exact Common App profile lists first-year SAT/ACT optional/flexible. SAT/ACT can still supply English-proficiency evidence; that requirement is separate. Undergraduate admission is women-centered with published eligibility conditions, unlike coeducational graduate programs; check eligibility at https://www.simmons.edu/admission-aid/application-process/international-applicants/undergraduate before applying.

english.value: Non-native speakers need proof. First-year exemption requires all secondary education (3–4 years) in English and no ESL/ELL classes in grades 11–12. Completing Kaplan Advanced Level is another alternative. Published tests: older TOEFL 83, Essentials 8, IELTS 6.5, DET 115, SAT EBRW 550, ACT English 21, PTE 55 or KiBT 83. No new TOEFL scale is given; confirm newer exams. Transfer/Dix/online college-credit alternatives are not first-year exemptions.

evidence.quote: who have not taken any ESL/ELL classes in 11th or 12th grades

fee.value: The exact institution-owned Common App profile lists no first-year application fee. Graduate/online fees, proficiency tests, visa, transcript evaluations and enrollment expenses are separate.

evidence.quote: Charges no application fee - First Year

deadline.value: First-year fall EA I/priority nursing November 1; EA II and Distinguished Scholar December 1; RD February 1, with RD decisions rolling February–April. These dates have no entry-year label; confirm the intended intake. First-year classification is age 23 or younger with 0–16 post-high-school credits. Transfer/adult and graduate schedules on the page are separate, not alternative first-year deadlines.
